previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for right-sided abdominal pain and nausea, occurring four days prior to admission. She has a history of gastric bypass and relies on tube feeds due to poor oral intake and post-surgical hypoglycemia. Initial management included NPO status and IV fluids. A CT scan ruled out bowel obstruction, showing the G-tube in correct position without signs of blockage. Tube feeds were restarted gradually and advanced to her baseline rate of 60 cc/hr, which she tolerated well. Pain and nausea were controlled throughout the stay. She was discharged home with home health services for wound care, continuing rifaximin, sucralfate, lansoprazole, docusate, and PRN Dilaudid. Follow-up was arranged with her surgeon.
